title: Spritesheets Schema
description: Schema for spritesheets using enum names as keys

sprites.description: Map of sprite enum names to their metadata

spriteMetadata.description: Metadata for a single sprite type

AbsoluteZOrder.description:
Absolute render order (draw lowest first): a non-zero entry replaces the sprite's base y entirely. Use large values (e.g. 10000, 100000) to always draw above or below the y-sorted world. Mutually exclusive with RelativeZOrder.

A value of 0, or an index past the end of the list, means 'no explicit zorder' for that sprite: it sorts at its base y. Omit both AbsoluteZOrder and RelativeZOrder to sort every sprite by its base y. The base y is the sprite's y-position, except walls which use their bottom edge (y + sprite height).

Indexing: one entry per sprite variant for obstacles and walls (the sprite index), one entry per grid cell for multiblocks (row-major: index = row * grid_size.x + col), and only entry [0] for everything else (NPCs, runes, gates, chests, etc.).

Any non-zero entry makes the sheet count as having an explicit zorder (SpriteSheet::has_zorder), which flight honours: a flying player stays behind it where their ground ordering would. Walls are always honoured in flight, whatever their zorder.

RelativeZOrder.description:
Relative render order (draw lowest first): a non-zero entry is added to the sprite's base y. Use small offsets (e.g. -16, 2, 48) to nudge a sprite's sorting line. Mutually exclusive with AbsoluteZOrder.

A value of 0, or an index past the end of the list, means 'no explicit zorder' for that sprite: it sorts at its base y. Omit both AbsoluteZOrder and RelativeZOrder to sort every sprite by its base y. The base y is the sprite's y-position, except walls which use their bottom edge (y + sprite height).

Indexing: one entry per sprite variant for obstacles and walls (the sprite index), one entry per grid cell for multiblocks (row-major: index = row * grid_size.x + col), and only entry [0] for everything else (NPCs, runes, gates, chests, etc.).

Any non-zero entry makes the sheet count as having an explicit zorder (SpriteSheet::has_zorder), which flight honours: a flying player stays behind it where their ground ordering would. Walls are always honoured in flight, whatever their zorder.

indices_per_sequence.description: How many 'sprite_indices' entries the animation loops over, one per animation frame. 1 = static sprite.

framerate.description: Animation framerate in frames per second. 0 = not animated. Use 0 for single-frame sprites.

grid_size.description: Width (x) and height (y) of the sprite, in grid cells

door_position.description: Grid cell of the multiblock's door, as a column (x) and row (y) within 'grid_size', counted from the top-left cell (0, 0). If omitted, defaults to (0, 0).

particle_offsets.description: Particle spawn points, as pixel offsets from the sprite's top-left corner. Optional. E.g. the graveyard altar's flame positions, one per relic sacrifice.

walking_collision_mask.description: Which cells of the sprite collide, one boolean per 'grid_size' cell in row-major order (left to right, top to bottom). For NPCs these are the cells it stands on, used for collision and pathfinding clearance. Shortcut: a single entry (e.g. [true]) applies that value to every cell, whatever the 'grid_size'. Otherwise there must be at least one entry per cell. If omitted, every cell collides. All false is valid: the sprite does not collide (an NPC then logs a warning at spawn and cannot touch the player).

flying_collision_mask.description: Which cells block the player while flying on the witchesbroom. Same format as walking_collision_mask: one boolean per grid_size cell in row-major order, or a single entry applied to every cell. If omitted, flight blocking falls back to the size-based rule (walls and multiblocks larger than 1x1 block, other sprites can be flown over).

sprite_indices.description: Array of sprite indices in the texture
